dedupe_keys.name: basel committee on banking supervision principles for operational resilience march 2021

description: These principles from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision set out a principles-based approach to improving the operational resilience of banks, meaning their ability to withstand operational risk events that could cause significant failures or wide-scale disruption in financial markets, such as pandemics, cyber incidents, technology failures or natural disasters. They build on the Committee's revised principles for the sound management of operational risk and draw on earlier guidance on corporate governance, outsourcing and business continuity. They were published by the Basel Committee at the Bank for International Settlements on 31 March 2021, after a consultative document in August 2020, and are listed as current. Coverage is international, for banking supervisors and banks worldwide. The 12-page PDF is available free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: they are high-level principles implemented differently by each jurisdiction, and they give no data or thresholds. For simulation they define what banks must keep running through disruptions, a basis for setting critical operations and recovery targets in financial infrastructure resilience scenarios. It is related to the Bank of England operational resilience of the financial sector record in this catalogue.
